steps.name: Joyous Lateran Citizen
steps.text: The town feels so lively today. is it because the conference is about to start?

steps.name: Relaxed Lateran Citizen
steps.text: Maybe. There are explosions everywhere. Everyone's so excited.

steps.name: Joyous Lateran Citizen
steps.text: Hey, what the hell?!

steps.name: Relaxed Lateran Citizen
steps.text: Is that... an executor... and a Legatus?!

steps.name: Joyous Lateran Citizen
steps.text: What's going on? A parkour competition?

steps.name: Relaxed Lateran Citizen
steps.text: That sounds like fun! Why don't you join in?

steps.name: Joyous Lateran Citizen
steps.text: Let's go! See if we can catch up with them!

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: This should be far enough...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: *Sigh*... You're a stubborn one, aren't you, Federico?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As are you.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I thought you didn't have a mission... Aren't you practically on vacation?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I don't get it. Is there a reason you can't get off my case? What did I ever do to offend you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: My last mission was in Siracusa, to recover the personal effects of a local Sankta.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Among them was a notebook. In it, he wrote that he once saw a female Sankta come into contact with a male Sarkaz.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Alright, I can see why you'd look into that, but what does it have to do with me? I'm decidedly male, in case you can't tell.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I followed all the leads I had and found the Sankta woman's address: 7-265 Via Thervatius, Pagus Stevonus.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: And when you made it there, you found that she'd already passed away.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That's correct.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: So you had no choice but to keep following her tracks. Then you found she had been taking suspicious trips, and that she always contacted a specific Legatus before she left on her journeys...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Hahahahaha, this is good. This is very good!

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: And here I thought I gave myself away in Victoria or left some evidence after I talked to Andoain. Never would I have thought it was because I helped Feoria out of the goodness of my heart.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: This might just be some kind of fate.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Are you done musing?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: *Sigh*, Federico, if my hunch's correct, you probably can't feel what I'm feeling right now. Yes? No?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes. And I do not care.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The emotions of those I arrest are not my concern.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Does that mean you care about the feelings of anyone you're not arresting?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You and I are the same. Neither of us cares for empathy... The way I see it, we could be great friends.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Actually, I think Laterano could use more people like you.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Someone who doesn't let their empathy get to them, always doing things by the book.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I don't disagree. Perhaps I could pay you a visit in the penitentiary after your trial and we could discuss it more.
So, that's your reason, Oren?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Well, here comes the worst of my troubles... Why must an honest-to-God good guy like me be blessed with such rotten luck?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Good day, Cardinal Velliv.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Good day, Executor Federico.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: The Seventh Tribunal will handle the traitor from this point forward. The Notarial Hall's involvement is concluded. Please send a copy of your report on this matter to both the Seventh and First Tribunals.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: This is my authorization code.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Confirmed. In accordance with all relevant regulations.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: So? Would you like to go back to your vacation or join me in arresting the Astray? It's up to you.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Vel, has anyone ever heard Federico say goodbye to anyone?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: You can stop trying to cozy up to me.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I thought you were here to help me.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: If you were here to arrest me, you could've waited until Federico was done, right?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Of course, it's possible that he couldn't take me... but that wouldn't mean you had to send him home, right?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I simply realized that you might be more useful than I expected.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: When I read Federico's report, I thought you were just Andoain's helping hand... but it looks like... you're not as much of an imbecile as I thought.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I'm honored.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Cecelia's existence is a threat to Laterano. You don't want this threat to be wiped away... not because you want to see it executed, but because you want to use it to make a deal.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: It really makes my heart ache, you know? It's such a windfall, but no one's trying to touch the pile of money.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I'm the most faithful to Laterano a man can be, honestly. You know that, Velliv.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I'm His Holiness's biggest supporter. His ideals, anyway.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: But you don't agree with the way he does things, correct?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Like this conference, for example. You don't think there's any point to it.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: And you think there is?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Velliv, how much do you know about Victoria these days?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You wouldn't understand just how close we are to war.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: And at a time like this, His Holiness put up all the political capital he accumulated over the last couple decades... but even though he managed to get most of the countries to bend, the envoys who showed up... they hardly have any weight.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: In more peaceful times, maybe we could use this as a foundation and slowly pave our way forward.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: But we don't live in peaceful times. There's no time for us to dilly-dally around if we actually want to see his ideals put into practice.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I saw a lot of even dirtier moves in Victoria, with my own eyes. I won't say it's the right way to do things, but if doing the right thing doesn't get us to the finish line—

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Tell me, would you rather be a woman of integrity?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: You know, you usually aren't this talkative in situations like these.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: What are you waiting for?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Actually, I just changed my mind.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: After traveling out there for so long, I'm buying less and less into the idea that Sankta are special.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: We've got the empathy thing, we feel what we feel. That's it.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What just happened, though... Even I have to admit... I felt something ancient and primal... and it originated in my heart.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Moreover, we got ourselves a trump card.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: All those envoys are gathered here in Laterano, and we are blessed with a miracle.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What does that mean? What could it mean? There is still a lot for us to do, isn't there?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I think you might be mistaken about one thing. You think there is no place for the Summit of Nations during troubled times... I suggest you look at this from the other side.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: That said, I think you have the right idea about one point. There are certain things that His Holiness can't do himself, and I also don't think there's any harm in having a backup plan.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: You're a lucky man, Oren. I do have a use for you.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Come out, Patia.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: At least you still have some sense in you, and your Sarkaz friends aren't running around the city, joining in on the commotion.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: If any of the envoys saw the Sarkaz actively sabotaging the Summit of Nations in Laterano... Things wouldn't end nearly as well.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: What are you trying to say?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Andoain is on his way to the Basilica, isn't he?

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: What do you know about him?!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I've got no reason to tell you, Patia.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: But before I go settle my score with him, I need you to stop the stupid, annoying little tricks.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: While your people might still have some sense in you and you aren't actually trying to sabotage the Summit of Nations...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I'm warning you. Don't push your luck. Things don't always go the way we want them to.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Oh? So now it's your turn to 'convince' me?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: This is just a little advice. If you don't want to take it, that's no feathers off my plumage.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Fiammetta, tell me. What are you thinking?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What else could I be thinking? I'm doing my job... I'm settling the score. It's not that complicated.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Why did you leave the Pontifica Cohors eight years ago?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: They don't get to leave the city, only the Notarial Hall does. What's it matter? Why ask about that?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I don't know what you're brooding about. Maybe you put your hopes on me for something, but I don't really get what your whole thing about Lateran Liberi is about.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: And I couldn't care less about it.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: A teammate I trusted betrayed us. One of my friends got hurt because of it, and another got exiled. There might even be traitors who have eyes on them because of it.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I made this mistake once... and I won't let it happen again.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I'll protect them. It's as simple as that.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: And I'm not going to apologize if that doesn't fit in with your fantasies.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: ...Pfft.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Don't get cocky, Mostima. In the same position, wouldn't you do the same?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You're right. I would.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: It's true. I've got a fantasy.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: But so what if it's a fantasy? Fantasies, ideals. If I didn't chase the things I once believed in, I wouldn't have made it this far.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Maybe I'm too naive to entrust others with my ideals, but I have no regrets.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I don't get you.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: That's why I'm not going to back down. Even if everything I'm doing seems stupid and annoying to you, it's my mission, and I will see it through to the end.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: If you want to stop me, you'll have to take me down.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Very well, Patia.
